title: feat(web): adds expiration and joined columns to the team table
description: ## What it solves Resolves: missing date context in the workspace Team tables, plus a set of responsive-layout bugs in the shared spaces table on mid-size screens. 1. Team members tables had no date columns — you couldn't see when a member joined, when an invite was sent, or when it expires. 2. On windows roughly between 768px and full screen, fixed-layout columns compressed below their content and painted over each other (e.g. the "Wallet sign-in" 2FA badge overlapping the Role column). 3. The network-logos pill in the address book wrapped its "+N" indicator onto a second row when the Chains column got tight. ## How this PR fixes it **Date columns (Team tables)** - Active members: sortable **Member since** column (`createdAt`, absolute date). - Pending invites: **Invited on** (absolute) and **Expires** (relative, "in 6 days") columns. - `formatDate` ('MMM d, yyyy') and `parseTimestamp` (safe ISO → timestamp, `null` for missing/invalid) are promoted to `@safe-global/utils/utils/date`; `TxDateLabel` now reuses `formatDate` instead of hardcoding the same schema. **Compact layout (shared `PaginatedDataTable`)** - Each column's `minWidth` now acts as a fit-floor contribution. The table measures its container (ResizeObserver) and, when the container is narrower than the summed minimums (or on phones), switches to the mobile presentation: secondary columns fold into the expandable row detail, layout falls back to auto — no horizontal scrolling, no overlap. Container-based (not a viewport breakpoint) so it adapts to the sidebar automatically. - Cell renderers receive `{ isCompact }`, so per-cell behaviors follow the same signal: members table (email under name, kebab actions), address book (short address, kebab actions — `SpaceAddressBookActions` takes it as a prop instead of `useIsMobile`). - Both address book tables' column widths summed to 110%, silently shrinking every column; rebalanced to 100% with Chains at a true 20%. - Capped network-logo lists (logos + "+N") no longer wrap; uncapped lists (safe-creation flows) keep wrapping. ## How to test it 1. Open a workspace → Team: active members show "Member since"; the Pending tab shows "Invited on" and "Expires" (dash when an invite has no expiry). All three sort. 2. Shrink the window through ~900px: no column overlap and no horizontal scrollbar — the date/email columns fold into a per-row "Show details" chevron; actions collapse into a kebab. 3. Workspace address book: Chains and Added by stay visible through mid-size widths, the logos pill never wraps, and everything folds into the row detail only when it genuinely no longer fits. 4. Transactions history: date group labels unchanged (same format, now via the shared util). Layout : ## Affected flows - Workspace admin reviews team members / pending invites (Team page tables) - Workspace address book browsing and pending address-book requests (compact behavior, widths, pill) - Transaction history date group labels (refactor only, same output) ## Blast radius - `PaginatedDataTable` (shared): consumed by `MembersList`, `SpaceAddressBookTable`, `PendingRequestsTable` — all three verified by their suites. `DataTableColumn.cell` gained an optional second argument (backward-compatible). - `@safe-global/utils/utils/date`: additive exports only (`formatDate`, `parseTimestamp`); shared with mobile but no existing function changed. - `NetworkLogosList` (multichain): no-wrap applies only to `showHasMore` (capped) usages; creation-flow full lists keep wrapping. - `SpaceAddressBookActions`: `isCompact` prop replaces internal `useIsMobile`. ## Risks / not checked - First paint on a mid-size window renders the full layout for one frame before the container measurement lands (same class of flash as existing `useIsMobile` behavior). - jsdom has no ResizeObserver — width-driven compact mode is tested via a mocked observer; real-browser resize behavior checked manually on Chrome only. - Address book `minWidth` floors (650px / 670px) tuned arithmetically; not verified on Firefox/Safari. - Not tested on mobile devices (only responsive mode). ## Visual summary ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before A1[table-fixed + % widths] --> B1[min-width ignored by fixed layout] B1 --> C1[columns overlap on mid-size screens] end subgraph After A2[ResizeObserver measures container] --> B2{container < Σ column minWidths?} B2 -->|no| C2[full column set, fixed layout] B2 -->|yes / phone| D2[compact: secondary columns fold into row detail, kebab actions, short addresses] end ``` ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 - [ ] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 - [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻 - [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯 --- ## CLA signature With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Agreement](https://safe.global/cla).

findings.claim: The test asserts `formatDate(new Date('2026-04-22T12:00:00.000Z').getTime())` equals `'Apr 22, 2026'`, but `date-fns` `format` uses local time, and since `packages/utils`'s test script runs bare `jest` with no `TZ` pin (unlike `apps/web`, which pins `TZ=CET`), the test would resolve to Apr 23 and fail in timezones at UTC+13/+14.

The new parseTimestamp helper duplicates an existing private helper elsewhere in the codebase, differing only in returning null versus undefined; now that a shared version exists, the local copy should be deleted and callers repointed to the package entrypoint.
The `hideClass` flash guard is `max-[767px]:hidden`, which only covers viewports below 768px, so it does not mask the new first-paint flash that can occur at ≥768px viewports with narrow containers.

The variant prop on MembersList has a default value even though its only consumer always passes the value explicitly at both call sites, so the default provides no benefit and only risks a future call site silently rendering the wrong content (e.g., "Member since" for pending invites) instead of failing type-check. The prop should be made required.
The code does not catch the exception that can be thrown here; it should be caught and null returned instead.

On a desktop viewport with a narrow container, `containerWidth` is `null` on first paint so `isCompact` evaluates to `false`, causing the full column set to render at full width before collapsing once the ResizeObserver fires, producing a layout flash.

The address column width changed from `width: '40%', minWidth: 360` to `width: hasMiddleColumn ? '30%' : '40%', minWidth: 240`, and because `md:table-fixed` CSS ignores `min-width` on cells, the minWidth no longer reserves space and only feeds the compact-mode threshold calculation.

There are two functions named formatDate with incompatible meanings inside features/spaces: one produces an absolute date and the other a relative date, and both are imported from sibling files in the same feature, so an IDE auto-import can silently pick the wrong one. This already forced a workaround in a new test that aliases one import and redeclares a local formatDate. One side should be renamed to disambiguate them.
The same address column width/minWidth regression present in SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx also exists here, risking address clipping without ellipsis at mid-width desktop containers.

The new `formatDate` utility (format `'MMM d, yyyy'`) has the same name as a pre-existing `formatDate` in `apps/web/src/features/spaces/utils.ts:72` (format `'Today at 9:41 AM'`), and both are now imported within the same `features/spaces` directory (`MembersList/index.tsx:2` uses the new one, `SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx:13` uses the old one), creating a same-name/different-behavior collision risk within one feature area.

The invariant that column widths must sum to 100% (stated at index.tsx:160) is enforced in two separate places 115 lines apart: `dateColumn` hardcodes `width: '15%'` while the other widths (`badgeWidth`/name/email) are computed from `isCondensed`, with nothing checking that they still total 100% if either side changes independently.

Before this change, the same 900px container gave the address 40% (360px) width, which fit; the diff both narrowed the share (40%→30%) and lowered the minWidth floor that would otherwise trigger compact/shortened-address mode, making this a regression for existing users rather than a pre-existing bug.

Two comments in PaginatedDataTable still describe the old mobile-only behavior model even though the code now behaves differently: one says the detail row is mobile-only when it now renders in any compact layout, and another calls minWidth a desktop-only floor when it now also drives the compact threshold. Nearby JSDoc comments were correctly updated in the same diff, but these two were missed.

The fix should either keep `shortAddress` enabled whenever the computed column width falls below ~330px, or raise `minWidth` back toward 330 so the table switches to compact mode before the address stops fitting.

`setContainerWidth(entry.contentRect.width)` stores the raw pixel width on every resize observer frame, causing a new state value and a full table re-render (up to pageSize 25 rows × 7 columns) on each frame, when only the boolean compact/non-compact threshold actually matters; storing `containerWidth < tableMinWidth` instead would limit re-renders to the two threshold-crossing transitions.

The compact-mode width threshold sums the minWidth of all columns including secondary ones, and this PR added two 110px date columns without revisiting existing 180px email and 130px 2FA minimums, pushing the total to about 900px for one configuration. Since the page content area sits inside a sidebar layout, common desktop viewports (1280px, 1024px) can fall under that threshold, causing columns to collapse into the compact view on ordinary desktops rather than only on mobile; this should be confirmed as intended or the column minWidths should be lowered.

Now that `SpaceAddressBookActions` collapses into a kebab menu when `isCompact` is true, local contacts remain the only rows in the same column still showing two raw icon buttons in compact mode, creating an inconsistent affordance; threading `isCompact` through `LocalContactActions` the same way would make it consistent.

A CSS class is applied whenever showHasMore is true, but the actual '+N' badge that the class is meant to support also requires networks.length to exceed maxVisible, so the class is being applied to lists where no '+N' badge is rendered, as shown by updated snapshots. This removes wrapping from those lists for no stated reason; the condition should be gated to match when '+N' actually renders, or the justifying comment should be reworded to match current behavior.

A full 42-character Safe address rendered with identicon and copy button needs about 330px, but between the compact threshold (~650px with a middle column) and ~1100px the table stays in full (non-compact) layout, giving the address only 30% of container width (e.g. 270px at 900px, 210px at 700px), which is too narrow to fit the address.

SrcEthHashInfo wraps the address in a `Box` with `overflow: hidden` and `textOverflow: ellipsis` applied only to the name box, not the address box, so when the address doesn't fit it is cut off mid-string with no ellipsis, silently dropping the trailing bytes of the address.
The fix is to assert against a locally-constructed date instead of a UTC ISO string, or to pin `TZ` for the workspace's test script.

The generated file docs/engineering/pr-self-review-checklist.generated.md is not covered by .gitignore even though it is meant to be gitignored by design, so it appears as an untracked file; the gitignore setup needs to be fixed when the docs/engineering directory is first committed.

A locally defined `const formatDate = (iso: string) => ...` shadows the imported `formatDate` that it wraps/aliases, which is confusing; renaming the local helper to `formatIso` would make the code clearer.
